Definition: must or fresh grape-juice (as just squeezed out); by implication (rarely) fermented wine
BiblicalUsage: New wine is the sign of a land doing well. When the commandment went abroad under Hezekiah the people brought in abundance the firstfruits of corn, wine and oil, and the Assyrian Rabshakeh tempts Jerusalem with a promise of a land of corn and wine, of bread and vineyards.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word shows how ordinary abundance becomes a spiritual sign: corn and wine in the storehouse mean a people blessed, and a land of corn and wine is what the enemy offers as a substitute for the Lord's own land.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
